source_of_truth: Read by hand: src/app/(workspace)/layout.tsx begins with the 'use client' directive, so the whole workspace subtree ships and renders as client JavaScript (a confirmed client-boundary-too-high on a layout). The same file gates UI with the literal comparison user.role === 'owner', a hardcoded role check in client UI code. src/components/Nav.tsx compares role === 'tablist', an ARIA role value, which is not a permission and must not be flagged.
provenance: blind generalization: truth derived from source without consulting tool output

expected.rationale: 'use client' at the top of a layout forces the entire workspace subtree onto the client; the directive is syntactically present on line 1.
user.role === 'owner' is a literal role comparison in UI code; permissions should come from a server-provided matrix, not a role string baked into the client.

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: role === 'tablist' compares an ARIA role value, not a permission; it is UI semantics, not authorization.
the page is a Server Component with no 'use client' directive.
